decision: Defined four storage POCs and standalone/three-process TCP matrices
why: Prior small-installation recommendation has no measurements; compare actual durable batches before choosing a high-volume layout

decision: Use a fixed-leader replication experiment, not custom Raft
why: Separate the empirical fan-out cost from consensus correctness; do not imply elections or HA from a throughput experiment
result: Production HA remains outside the POC claim

decision: Added serial workload orchestration, raw latency retention, reopened payload audits, and summary gates
why: Measurements need a rerunnable contract that rejects missing bytes and bookmarks rather than trusting live counters
result: Python evidence assertions pass; runtime integration pending

decision: Rejected initial engine ranking and enabled RocksDB full synchronization on macOS
why: Rust used F_FULLFSYNC but the bundled C++ build used plain fsync; the faster result changed the durability contract
result: Initial smoke is correctness-only; rebuild and rerun required

decision: Completed normalized smoke runs and all workspace correctness tests
why: Actual reopened bytes and retained bookmark positions must agree before measuring speed
result: 8 smoke configurations verified; 30 Rust and 4 Python tests passed

decision: Aborted the first main run when its executable exposed the old bookmark limit
why: A source-level test pass did not prove the release executable was current; add a build-before-run gate
result: No failed-run data used in rankings

decision: Completed 72 normalized trials across four stores and one/three-node configurations
why: Measure the original redb preference against actual full-synchronization batching and sharding results
result: Fjall leads the tested 128-record three-node cases; all reopened replica audits matched

decision: Expanded Fjall and RocksDB to 1/2/4/8 shards and 128/512-record batches
why: The first matrix shows batching and independent writer paths matter; measure their configuration tradeoff with longer repeats

decision: Stopped sustained matrix when Fjall lost its fixed-leader acknowledgement quorum
why: At about 39 MiB per shard, multi-second stalls exceeded the peer deadline; a success-only summary would hide the failure
result: NOT VERIFIED: preserve the negative result and investigate

decision: Strengthened failure evidence gates and source preservation
why: Require an explicit zero-ack quorum rejection and verify the prefix digest even when an unacknowledged tail exists; keep failed scratch and reproducible sources
result: Six Python evidence tests passed; source checkpoint captured

decision: Reconciled the failure artifacts with stronger zero-ack and prefix-digest gates
why: A nonzero exit or a longer recovered tail alone was not enough evidence
result: All four historical failure scenarios satisfy the stronger assertions

decision: Completed scaling, message-size, and all planned sustained observations including the failed attempt
why: Record sizes change the storage ranking; preserve the failure instead of pooling only successful rates
result: 138 successful short/scale/size trials; sustained Fjall 2 successes and 1 failure, RocksDB 3 successes

decision: Replaced the small-installation global-writer proposal with a high-volume sharded LSM direction
why: Measured batching and writer-path scaling favor LSM finalists, while sustained failures and message-size results prevent a universal winner claim
result: Updated proposal; original preserved as initial-proposal.md

decision: Added a controlled slow-follower admission experiment
why: Blocking enqueue to every bounded peer queue can throttle a healthy majority; compare isolation without weakening durable acknowledgement
result: Implementation and targeted test in progress

decision: Prefer RocksDB for the next high-volume baseline, with Fjall retained as a challenger
why: At the largest five-second configuration RocksDB kept about 96 percent of throughput with much lower batch p99; larger records and sustained completion also favor caution
result: Provisional next-iteration choice, not production certification

decision: Removed one redundant segment-repair comment after independent comment review
why: The committed extent checks and diagnostic already express the rule; no runtime behavior changed
result: One comment removed; original source preserved in source-checkpoint

decision: Completed six real-node slow-minority comparisons and preserved durable majority rejection
why: Nonblocking isolation removes the all-peer queue coupling while retaining local plus follower durability; excluded peer has no catch-up claim
result: Three repeats per policy passed; controlled completion about 0.245s versus 4.920s

decision: Repeated all backend topologies and failure scenarios after the isolation change
why: Check the final executable and stronger evidence assertions, not just the baseline source
result: Final runtime and unit-test gates passed

decision: Completed independent final evidence review and left no POC servers or scratch data running
why: The reviewer reconciled all six isolation results and the zero-ack failure evidence; remaining limits stay explicit
result: VERIFIED for the stated POC boundary; production HA and original sustained failure remain open
